data.name: Tarsion
data.gender_notes: Tarsion is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word ‘tarsos’ meaning ‘stone’ or ‘rock’. In the Bible, Tarsion could refer to various places, such as the city of Tarsus, where Paul was born, or the name of a stone or rock. The name Tarsion carries the meaning “Stone, Rock” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Tarsion usually hope their child will grow to embody stone, rock and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Tarsion belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Stone, Rock.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tarsion total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Ταρσίων
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ταρσίων προέρχεται από την πόλη Ταρσού, στην Κιλικία, και συσχετίζεται με την περιοχή της Κιλικίας. Ο Ταρσίων ήταν ένας από τους σπουδαίους μαθητές του Αποστόλου Παύλου και είχε ένα ιδιαίτερο ρόλο στην εκκλησία της Κιλικίας. Το όνομα του Ταρσίων συνδέεται επίσης με την ιδιότητα του αποστόλου και της αποστολικής αποστολής.

in_latin.name: Tarsion
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Tarsionem a civitate Tarsus, in Cilicia, ortam derivatur et cum regione Ciliciae associatur. Tarsion unus ex discipulis Apostoli Pauli et in ecclesia Ciliciae functus est. Nomen Tarsionis cum apostolatus et apostolicae missionis officio connectitur.

in_english.name: Tarsion
in_english.meaning: from Tarsus, a city of Cilicia, Tarsion, a disciple of Apostle Paul
in_english.long_meaning: The name Tarsion originates from the city of Tarsus in Cilicia, and is associated with the region of Cilicia. Tarsion was one of the esteemed disciples of Apostle Paul and played a unique role in the church of Cilicia. The name Tarsion is also connected with the apostolate and the apostolic mission.

historical_references.reference: Tarsius, the legendary founder of Tarsus, was a Hittite prince who supposedly converted to Christianity and was martyred for his faith. According to tradition, he was the son of King Tarcondemus of Cilicia and was sent to Rome to be educated. There, he was converted to Christianity by the apostles Peter and Paul. After returning to Tarsus, he was persecuted for his faith and was eventually killed by the Romans in the late 1st or early 2nd century.
historical_references.context: Legendary founder of Tarsus, converted to Christianity and martyred for his faith

Many early Christian saints and martyrs are believed to have lived and died in Tarsus, contributing to its Christian heritage. This theory does not have a specific time period associated with it, as it refers to the general history of Tarsus as a Christian center.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Tarsion' is of Christian origin and is believed to have derived from the biblical name Tarsis, which is mentioned in the Old Testament. In modern contexts, this name has gained popularity in various role-playing games, particularly Dungeons & Dragons and Pathfinder. In these games, Tarsion is often used as the name of a character, NPC, or location. The name has also found its way into the World of Darkness RPG, where it can be used as a personal name for a vampire or other supernatural creature. Overall, the use of Tarsion in these platforms reflects a growing interest in Christian folklore and mythology within the gaming community.
